subtopics.title: The Three Questions and the Test They Set

questions.question: Every economic system must answer which three questions?
options: WHAT to produce, HOW to produce it, and FOR WHOM to produce
When to save, when to spend and when to borrow

questions.question: The master variable that divides one economic system from another is:
options: Who owns and controls the MEANS OF PRODUCTION, since ownership carries the right to decide

questions.question: In a country with millions of job-seekers, the HOW question carries special weight because:
options: Machines are unavailable in poor countries
The WHAT question no longer applies
Choosing between labour-intensive and capital-intensive methods determines how many people are employed
Wages are set by the constitution

questions.question: An economic system should not be confused with a political system because:
options: Political systems do not affect economies
Economies are classified by ownership and co-ordination, while political orders are classified by how power is won and held — separate axes

questions.question: The price mechanism co-ordinates a free market by a process in which:
options: Rising demand lifts price, higher price fattens profit, profit pulls in producers and resources, and supply expands — the price carrying both information and incentive
The state gazettes maximum prices each quarter
Producers meet annually to fix prices
Prices are chosen by the largest firm

questions.question: In a pure free market, FOR WHOM is answered by:
options: An assessment of each household's need
INCOME — output flows to purchasing power

questions.question: A pure market barely supplies police patrols and lighthouses because they are:
options: PUBLIC GOODS — non-excludable, so nobody pays for them voluntarily

questions.question: A smelter that pollutes the neighbourhood's air is a market failure because:
options: The harm it causes appears nowhere in its costs, so its price understates true cost and its output is too large

questions.question: Under central planning, WHAT to produce is decided by:
options: The planning authority, according to its reading of social need

questions.question: A genuine, fairly stated strength of central planning is that:
options: It generates the widest product variety
Resources can be swung rapidly behind one national goal, and basic needs can be guaranteed regardless of earnings

questions.question: The INFORMATION problem of planning is that:
options: The local facts about wants and costs held by millions of people cannot be collected by any central office, while market prices summarise them automatically

questions.question: Planned economies produce queues for some goods and warehouses of others because:
options: Administered prices cannot move, so the error signals that a market price would send never fire and mistakes go uncorrected

subtopics.title: The Mixed and Dualistic Economy — South Africa

questions.question: In a mixed economy, FOR WHOM is answered by:
options: Market income first, then MODIFIED by redistribution — progressive tax, grants, free basic services and no-fee schools

questions.question: Which combination identifies South Africa as a MIXED economy?
options: State ownership of every farm and factory
Property rights beside socio-economic rights in the Constitution, mostly private production beside state-owned utilities, market regulators, and heavy redistribution
Prices set annually by a planning ministry

questions.question: Calling an economy DUALISTIC means that:
options: A formal, modern, capital-intensive economy and an informal, survivalist one operate side by side within one country
Its imports and exports are equal

questions.question: The structural causes of South Africa's dualism include:
options: Land dispossession and migrant labour, apartheid spatial planning that settled people far from work, engineered inequality in schooling, and the collateral wall that blocks credit

subtopics.title: Three Ways to Run the Kitchen

questions.question: The food stalls along the fence — where the sold-out amagwinya table brings two stands next Saturday — represent:
options: The free market — prices talk, profit motivates, and your pocket decides your plate

questions.question: The organisers' tent — one committee, one pot of curry, every player fed free — represents:
options: The centrally planned economy — fairer plates, blinder cooking

questions.question: A tournament running the free meal tent AND the stalls at the same time models:
options: The MIXED economy — which is what South Africa runs

subtopics.title: What the Till Knows and the Memo Doesn't

questions.question: "A price is a message" means:
options: Every sale and every sold-out table transmits a fact about what people want and what is scarce — millions of signals a day, gathered automatically and free
Prices are announced on the radio

questions.question: A planner's wrong guess persists because:
options: Planners are forbidden to change plans
The office fixed the price in advance, so the price cannot flag the error the way a market price would
Consumers adjust their wants to the plan

questions.question: The market's one deafness is that:
options: It reacts too slowly to demand
It hears only money — the hungry kid with empty pockets transmits no signal, which is why every country pitches a free meal tent beside its stalls

questions.question: The Rosebank fintech office and the fruit crate at the Tembisa taxi rank together illustrate:
options: Dualism — a formal, capital-rich economy and an informal, survivalist one in the same country

questions.question: The fruit seller cannot simply borrow money and expand because:
options: Banks lend against collateral, and someone with no assets to pledge cannot borrow the stock money that would let her grow
The law forbids lending to traders

questions.question: "One side worked harder" fails as an explanation of dualism because:
options: Nobody works hard in either economy
Effort is identical everywhere by law
The real walls are structural — confiscated and concentrated ownership, distance from workplaces, engineered schooling gaps and the collateral wall — none about effort
Hard work is impossible to observe

questions.question: Grants, no-fee schools, free basic services, land reform, township enterprise finance and commuter transport are best understood as:
options: Signs of a fully planned economy
The mixed economy's deliberate attempts to cut doors through the walls between the two economies
